This vignette covers the helpers for setting up a study, importing and
checking data, and recoding and summarising variables. They follow the steps
of the pipeline described in
`vignette("data_analysis_pipeline", package = "C306")`.

| Step | Functions |
|---|---|
| Set up a project | `createProject()` |
| Import a data dictionary | `import.info()`, `convert.info()` |
| Format and check data | `myformat.data()`, `inspect.data()`, `getlabel()` |
| Recode and reorder | `simple_recode()`, `simple_relevel()`, `simple_sort()`, `ref_lv()` |
| Derive and summarise | `mutate_f()`, `summarise_f()`, `labAE()`, `contSummary()`, `pct()` |

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(C306)
```

The examples use `baseline_data` and `ae_data`, a **simulated** two-arm trial
bundled with the package.

## Set up a project: `createProject()`

`createProject()` copies a standard folder structure, with template scripts
for importing, cleaning, analysing and reporting, into a new folder and adds an
RStudio project file. It refuses to write into a folder that is not empty.

```{r}
proj <- file.path(tempdir(), "myStudy")
createProject(proj)
list.files(proj, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(proj, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Import a data dictionary

### `import.info()`

OUCRU data dictionaries are Excel files with a `CRFs` sheet, a `Grids` sheet
and one sheet per CRF. `import.info()` reads the requested sheets and saves one
data frame per sheet, `<sheet>_info`, in an `.RData` file. A grid is requested
as `<CRF>_<Grid>`. The package includes a small example dictionary:

```{r}
dict <- system.file("extdata", "oucru_dictionary.xlsx", package = "C306")
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".RData")
import.info(c("ENR", "LAB", "LAB_G1"), input = dict, output = out)
load(out)
sheet_info_name
ENR_info
```

### `convert.info()`

`convert.info()` turns an OUCRU dictionary and its category list into the
general dictionary format used by `myformat.data()` and `inspect.data()`, with
columns `varname`, `label`, `type`, `unit`, `value`, `levels` and `missing`:

```{r}
oucru_info <- data.frame(
  Category = c(NA, "SEX"), Variable = c("AGE", "SEX"), Caption = c("Age", "Sex"),
  `Data type` = c("Integer", "RadioList"), Format = NA, check.names = FALSE
)
oucru_category <- data.frame(category = "SEX", submissionvalue = c("1", "2"),
                             text = c("Male", "Female"))
convert.info(oucru_info, oucru_category)
```

## Format and check data

### `myformat.data()`

`myformat.data()` applies a dictionary to raw data: it converts types, turns
codes into labelled factor levels, parses dates, sets missing-value codes to
`NA` and stores labels and units as attributes. Each row of the dictionary
describes one variable:

- `type`: `numeric`, `factor`, `character` or `datetime`
- `value`: the code-to-label map of a factor (`1='Male';2='Female'`), the
  date format of a datetime (`ymd`), or the allowed range of a number
  (`0;100`, used by `inspect.data()`)
- `levels`: the order of the factor levels
- `missing`: codes that mean missing, e.g. `-99`

Here we take a few columns of the simulated trial and introduce two errors:
an age of 150 and an ASA status of 4.

```{r}
raw <- head(baseline_data[, c("usubjid", "age", "asa", "timetoadm")], 8)
raw$age[3] <- 150
raw$asa[5] <- 4
raw$timetoadm[6] <- -99

info <- data.frame(
  varname = c("usubjid", "age", "asa", "timetoadm"),
  label = c("Participant ID", "Age", "ASA physical status", "Time to admission"),
  type = c("character", "numeric", "factor", "numeric"),
  unit = c(NA, "years", NA, "days"),
  value = c(NA, "0;100", "1='ASA I';2='ASA II';3='ASA III'", "0;60"),
  levels = c(NA, NA, "'ASA I';'ASA II';'ASA III'", NA),
  missing = c(NA, NA, NA, "-99")
)

dat <- myformat.data(raw, info)
str(dat)
```

The warning flags the ASA code that is not in the dictionary; it is kept as
an extra level so that it can be reported.

### `inspect.data()`

`inspect.data()` checks formatted data against the dictionary and lists
values out of range, codes not in the dictionary and missing values. The list
is returned and also written to `<prefix>_error.csv` in `outdir`
(`plot = TRUE` also saves the distribution of each variable to a PDF).

```{r}
inspect.data(dat, info, id = "usubjid", outdir = tempdir())
```

### `getlabel()`

`getlabel()` returns the label of a variable, with its unit, from its
attributes or from a dictionary. With `fit = TRUE` it describes the variable
as it enters a model, using the `scale` attribute (e.g. "per 10 years"):

```{r}
wt <- structure(c(60, 72), label = "Weight", unit = "kg", scale = 10)
getlabel(wt)
getlabel(wt, fit = TRUE)

meta <- data.frame(varname = c("age", "sex"), label = c("Age", "Sex"),
                   unit = c("years", NA), scale = c(10, NA),
                   type = c("numeric", "factor"))
getlabel("age", meta = meta)
getlabel(baseline_data[, c("age", "sex")], meta = meta)
```

## Recode and reorder

### `simple_recode()`

`simple_recode()` recodes values that match regular expressions; values that
match no pattern are kept. A pattern of `NA` recodes missing values.

```{r}
simple_recode(c("yes", "Yes", "no", NA),
              map = list(Y = "^[Yy]es$", N = "^no$", Unknown = NA))
```

A factor stays a factor, and `as` converts the result. For a data frame,
give one map per variable:

```{r}
recoded <- simple_recode(head(baseline_data[, c("sex", "vaso")]),
                         sex = list(Female = "^F$", Male = "^M$"),
                         vaso = list(Yes = "^Y$", No = "^N$"))
recoded
```

### `simple_relevel()`

`simple_relevel()` orders the levels of one variable to follow another
factor. For example, to list AE terms grouped by organ class in the order of
the classes:

```{r}
grp <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "group_data.csv", package = "C306"))
grp$class <- factor(grp$class)
grp2 <- simple_relevel(grp, ctcaename, by = class)
head(levels(grp2$ctcaename))
```

For a vector, give the grouping factor and a `map` from each group to its
values:

```{r}
simple_relevel(c("p", "q", "r"), by = factor(c("B", "A", "B"), levels = c("B", "A")),
               map = list(A = "q", B = c("p", "r")), value = "levels")
```

### `simple_sort()`

`simple_sort()` sorts a vector in a user-defined order:

```{r}
simple_sort(c("III", "I", "II", "I"), order = c("I", "II", "III"))
```

### `ref_lv()`

`ref_lv()` gets the reference (first) level of a factor, and `ref_lv<-` sets
it while keeping the order of the other levels:

```{r}
arm <- factor(baseline_data$Arm)
ref_lv(arm)
ref_lv(arm) <- "Sham procedure"
levels(arm)
```

## Derive and summarise

### `mutate_f()` and `summarise_f()`

These work like `dplyr::mutate()` and `dplyr::summarise()` but can create
several columns in one expression, with `c(...) := list(...)` in
`mutate_f()` and a named list in `summarise_f()`. They work on data frames,
grouped tibbles and data.tables.

```{r}
small <- head(baseline_data[, c("usubjid", "Arm", "maxhr", "minhr")], 6)
small %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Arm) %>%
  mutate_f(c("hr_range", "hr_mid") := list(maxhr - minhr, (maxhr + minhr) / 2))

baseline_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Arm) %>%
  summarise_f(list(n = length(age), mean_age = mean(age), max_sofa = max(sofa, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

### `labAE()`

For laboratory adverse events graded at each visit, `labAE()` flags the
visits where a new event should be reported: the grade reaches `gradecut` and
is higher than the worst grade so far.

```{r}
labAE(c(0, 1, 3, 3, 2, 4), gradecut = 3)

visits <- data.frame(id = rep(c("SIM-001", "SIM-002"), each = 3),
                     grade = c(1, 3, 3, 3, 2, 4))
visits %>%
  dplyr::group_by(id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(new_ae = labAE(grade, gradecut = 3))
```

### `contSummary()`

`contSummary()` formats summary statistics of a numeric vector as text. The
`statistics` string is a template: the words `mean`, `sd`, `median`, `Q1`,
`Q3`, `min` and `max` (in any case) are replaced by their values and all
other text is kept. This is what `sstable.baseline()` uses for continuous
variables.

```{r}
contSummary(baseline_data$bmi, "mean (sd)")
contSummary(baseline_data$age, "median (Q1-Q3)", digits = 0)
contSummary(baseline_data$icudays, "Median [IQR: Q1-Q3], range min-max", digits = 0)
```

### `pct()`

`pct()` returns proportions: the percentage of `TRUE` for a logical vector,
one per level for a factor, or one per interval for a number cut at `breaks`.

```{r}
pct(baseline_data$vaso == "Y")
pct(factor(baseline_data$ablettscore))
pct(baseline_data$age, method = "cont", breaks = c(0, 40, 60, 100))
```
